narrative.synopsis: Uranus refuses to let his fearsome children emerge and forces them back into Gaia. Gaia’s pain turns maternity into rebellion as she prepares a sickle and calls on her children for help.
narrative.openingSituation: The first divine household is ruled by Uranus, who will not tolerate children who frighten him.
narrative.centralConflict: Gaia is crushed by the children hidden inside her while Uranus keeps his dominance.
narrative.resolution: Gaia arms a plan of revolt and Cronus becomes the child ready to carry it out.
narrative.outcome: The conflict moves from silent imprisonment to open succession violence.

events.consequence: The Cyclopes are hidden away instead of honored as children.
The Hundred-Handers are forced into Gaia’s depths.
Gaia’s body bears the pain of Uranus’ control.
Gaia prepares the sickle and seeks an attacker.
Cronus agrees to act where the others hesitate.
